quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed by closing the throttle. Move your weight forward and down, then pull off the road. Do not brake, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use hard pressure on the front brake to keep the front tire from locking.
Use only one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the front brake lever gradually to avoid locking the front wheel. Use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: When another vehicle follows you too closely, what should you do?

options.text: Stay focused on the road ahead and ignore them.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to let a tailgater pass. Speeding up will only make them follow you at a higher speed and increase danger. Never ride on the shoulder because other drivers do not expect you there and may suddenly leave the road.

questions.question: Convex mirrors make cars look:
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away.
questions.explanation: Curved convex mirrors show a wider view of the road than flat mirrors. However, they make objects look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: What do goggles protect?

options.text: Your face but not your eyes.
Your eyes but not your face.
Neither your eyes nor your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your eyes but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. A face shield is needed to protect your entire face during a crash.

questions.question: Which body part operates the gearshift lever?
questions.correctAnswerText: Your left foot.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is located in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot. Know where all your motorcycle controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: In a position where the driver can see you.
Always on the far left side of the lane.
Always on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a position where the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when behind a car. This position makes you most visible in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good way to increase your visibility?

options.text: Wearing bright clothing with reflective material.
Using your headlight at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Waving at other drivers.
questions.explanation: To be visible, wear bright clothing with reflective material, use your headlight at all times, and use your signals and brake light correctly. Waving at drivers is not an effective visibility technique.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch located?
questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right handgrip.
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is next to the right handgrip. Learn where all your motorcycle controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: What is an advantage of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You will see less of the road and stay more focused.
You will have more time to react to what other vehicles do.
You can more easily follow the next vehicle's path.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to react to what other vehicles do.
questions.explanation: Space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you a clearer view of hazards, more time to react to them, and more room to maneuver around them.

questions.question: Your motorcycle is weaving while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Move to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle may weave over rain grooves or bridge gratings, but this is not dangerous. Stay calm and ride straight at a steady speed. Weaving to match the motion will make things worse.

questions.question: A tire goes flat while you are riding. What should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Use the good tire's brake and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the good tire's brake and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly and slow down by releasing the throttle. If you must brake, gradually use the brake on the good tire. Move toward the side of the road as you slow down, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: Your motorcycle helmet was in a crash. What should you do with it?
questions.correctAnswerText: Replace it.
questions.explanation: Replace your helmet after any crash. A helmet that has been in a crash cannot protect you properly.

questions.question: Before you ride, what should you check about your brakes?

options.text: They make a loud squeaking noise.
They create friction with the steering.
Each one can hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each one can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Test each brake lever before every ride. Make sure each one feels firm and can hold the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs and other rule signs are rectangular. They are white with black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In risky areas like intersections, shopping areas, school zones, and construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and both brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to danger.

questions.question: What color are warning signs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert riders to upcoming road hazards and conditions.

questions.question: Which riding formation keeps group riders closest together?
questions.correctAnswerText: Staggered.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets a group stay close while giving each rider safe distance from others. Use single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: How long can marijuana affect your ability to ride?
questions.correctAnswerText: More than six hours.
questions.explanation: When smoked, marijuana can affect you within minutes and last two to four hours. When eaten, it may take over an hour to start working, but effects can last more than six hours.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Adjust your lane position as conditions change.
Ride faster than usual to reach your destination quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight for better vision.
Stay very close to the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust your lane position as conditions change.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to adjust your lane position, especially at night. Use extra caution and safe riding skills when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: What should an experienced rider do?

options.text: Move to different positions in their lane based on road and traffic conditions.
Stay in the same part of the lane at all times.
Weave back and forth within the lane to be more visible.
Ride only on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to different positions in their lane based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle rider can use three different positions within their lane. Choose the safest position based on current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes firmly at the same time. Do not panic if the brakes lock.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When there are only a few vehicles on the road.
When drivers are following the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road is slippery.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more space to stop. This includes slippery pavement, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy and a driver might cut in front of you.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help protect you from serious injury?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ear buds.
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves. Ear buds do not provide protection.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with other drivers mean?

options.text: It is the best way to know that they see you.
It is not worth the effort.
It does not guarantee that they will yield to you when they should.
It guarantees that they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee that they will yield to you when they should.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but do not notice them.
